1.title: Responding in Defender XDR (3): Incidents, UEBA, Security Copilot and Complex Attacks
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Responding in Defender X D R (three): Incidents, you ee bee ay, Security Copilot and Complex Attacks. It covers the exam area two. Respond to security incidents. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Investigate and remediate alerts and incidents identified by Microsoft Sentinel. Investigate incidents by using agentic A I, including embedded Microsoft Security Copilot. Investigate complex attacks, such as multi-stage, multi-domain and lateral movement. Manage security incidents by using case management. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Respond to security incidents (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Managing incidents (case management)
1.text: Managing incidents (case management). The figure shows this: The attack story combines the alert story and the incident graph.

1.title: Managing incidents (case management), continued
1.text: Managing incidents (case management). Incident page tabs. Attack story, Alerts, Activities, Assets, Investigations, Evidence and Response, Summary, Similar incidents. Assets. Devices, Users, Mailboxes, Apps, Cloud resources. Status. Active (default), In progress, Resolved (needs a resolution note; also resolves linked active alerts). Classification. Not set, True positive (with threat type), Informational, expected activity (security tests, red team, expected behavior), False positive. Owner. One user or group.

1.title: Managing incidents (case management), continued
1.text: Managing incidents (case management). Tags. Custom tags and system tags (attack type, automatic investigation or disruption, Defender Experts, critical assets). Comments. Up to thirty thousand characters each, kept in the Activities log. Tasks. A checklist for the incident; created by hand or by a Sentinel automation rule.

1.title: Managing incidents (case management), continued
1.text: Managing incidents (case management). Incident cases (preview, the recommended experience) are found under Cases, then Incident. A case has an overview with a Copilot summary and attack graph, plus Alerts, Assets, Investigations, Evidence, Activities, Similar cases and Comments and attachments. Alerts can be moved between cases. Permissions: Security Data Read to view, Security Data Manage to change. Exam tip: Resolve with a classification. A sanctioned penetration test is Informational, expected activity, not false positive.

1.title: Investigating complex attacks
1.text: Investigating complex attacks. A multi-stage, multi-domain attack touches several products. Defender X D R correlates alerts from endpoint, email, identity, cloud apps and cloud workloads into one incident. Alert story. What happened, Actions taken, Related events. Incident graph. Entities and alerts over time; filter by severity, status and service source; hide entity types. Go hunt. All activity, Related alerts, All user anomalies (preview, last thirty days, needs you ee bee ay). Blast radius. The top eight attack paths from a selected node to critical targets.

1.title: Investigating complex attacks, continued
1.text: Investigating complex attacks. Blast radius extends and replaces attack path analysis. Prerequisites: Sentinel data lake onboarding and Exposure management (read). Path limits: up to seven hops from the source, five hops in cloud, five on-premises and three hybrid. It shows possible paths, not guaranteed ones, and only nodes inside your R back scope. Exam tip: Lateral movement equals follow the incident graph from the first compromised device to the next. Blast radius equals what the attacker could reach next.

1.title: Investigating Sentinel incidents
1.text: Investigating Sentinel incidents. You need Microsoft Sentinel Responder (guest users who assign incidents also need Directory Reader). Overview. Incident timeline, Similar incidents (up to twenty), Entities, Top insights. Entities tab. Info, Timeline (previous seven days of alerts, bookmarks, anomalies), Insights. Investigation graph. Needs entity mappings; works for incidents up to thirty days old; has exploration queries and a parallel timeline. Buttons. Tasks, Activity log, Logs; actions Run playbook, Create automation rule. Comments. thirty thousand characters each, one hundred per incident; only the author edits; delete needs Sentinel Contributor.

1.title: User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA)
1.text: User and entity behavior analytics (you ee bee ay). you ee bee ay builds behavioral baselines and scores anomalies. Enable it in the Defender portal: System, then Settings, then Microsoft Sentinel, then you ee bee ay, turn on you ee bee ay, sync Active Directory (needs Defender for Identity) and Microsoft Entra I D, then turn on Anomalies. There is no license cost, only storage.

1.title: User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), continued
1.text: User and entity behavior analytics (you ee bee ay). Identity Info. Entity profiles from Entra and optionally A D. Behavior Analytics. Deviations and Investigation Priority (zero to ten, event level, near real time). User Peer Analytics. Top twenty peers per user. Anomalies. Anomaly Score (zero to one, behavior level, batch).

1.title: Security Copilot and agentic AI
1.text: Security Copilot and agentic A I. Microsoft Security Copilot is embedded in the Defender portal and gives generative A I help during an investigation. Summarize incidents. Summary of up to one hundred alerts; cached for one week. Guided response. Suggested next actions. Analyze files and scripts. Explains what a file or script does. Generate K Q L queries for hunting. Natural language to K Q L. Create incident reports, summarize devices and identities. Reports and asset summaries.

1.title: Security Copilot and agentic AI, continued
1.text: Security Copilot and agentic A I. Agents work on their own for a defined task: Security Alert Triage Agent (phishing and other alert triage, preview), Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent, Threat Hunting Assistant, Security Analyst Agent, Dynamic Threat Detection Agent. For Entra: Conditional Access Optimization Agent and Identity Risk Management Agent. Agents are not enabled automatically; each is set up (often by a Security Administrator).

1.title: Security Copilot and agentic AI, continued
1.text: Security Copilot and agentic A I. Included capacity. Microsoft three sixty-five E five and E seven: four hundred security compute units (S C Us) per month per one thousand paid licenses, up to ten thousand per month; resets monthly, no rollover. Other customers. Provision one to one hundred S C Us, billed hourly. Copilot roles. Security Copilot Owner (capacity, usage, data sharing) and Contributor (sessions, promptbooks); these are Copilot roles, not Entra roles. Embedded access. Also needs the product role (for example a unified R back role with Security Copilot permission). Exam tip: Copilot summarizes and suggests; the analyst decides. Agents must be set up. S C Us measure usage and E five includes a monthly allowance.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An incident came from a sanctioned red team exercise. How should the analyst close it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Resolve it as informational, expected activity, with security test selected. Sanctioned tests are classified as Informational, expected activity with the activity type for security tests.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An analyst must trace how an attacker moved from a phished mailbox to a server across several products. Which tool gives the best view? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The Attack story and incident graph of the incident. The attack story and incident graph show correlated alerts and entities across domains over time.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A sock wants to use blast radius in an incident. Which two prerequisites apply? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A Sentinel data lake onboarding and Exposure management (read). Blast radius uses the Sentinel data lake and graph and needs Exposure management (read) or higher.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An analyst wants a numeric priority from zero to ten for unusual user activity in Sentinel. Which table holds it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Behavior Analytics, which holds Investigation Priority. Behavior Analytics has the Investigation Priority score from zero to ten.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An organization has Microsoft three sixty-five E five and five thousand paid licenses. How much Security Copilot capacity is included per month? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: two thousand security compute units, from four hundred per one thousand licenses. E five includes four hundred S C Us per one thousand licenses per month, so five thousand licenses give two thousand.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. The investigation graph button does not work for a Sentinel incident. What are likely causes? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The incident has no entity mappings or is older than thirty days. The graph needs entity mappings and supports incidents up to thirty days old.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which classification fits a sanctioned penetration test? Answer: Informational, expected activity. Question two. How many attack paths does blast radius show? Answer: The top eight. Question three. Which role investigates Sentinel incidents? Answer: Microsoft Sentinel Responder.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the range of Investigation Priority? Answer: zero to ten. Question five. What do E five customers receive per one thousand licenses? Answer: four hundred S C Us per month. Question six. Are Security Copilot agents enabled automatically? Answer: No, each must be set up.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Incident states: Active, In progress, Resolved; classify before resolving. Attack story: alert story plus incident graph; Go hunt. Blast radius: top eight paths; Sentinel data lake and Exposure management (read). Sentinel investigation: Responder; graph needs entity mappings, thirty days. you ee bee ay: Identity Info, Behavior Analytics (zero to ten), User Peer Analytics, Anomalies (zero to one). Copilot: summary of one hundred alerts, K Q L generation, agents set up by hand.
